mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when this trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing companies and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) where PAYEMS grows below 1% month-over-month while UNRATE falls below 5% signals a mismatch in labor market data, often preceding a revision or data error, which historically has coincided with increased market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 1% and UNRATE < 5% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant negative mean return over the 5-day horizon in triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equity sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month averages in the same quarter indicates a broad-based demand recovery, which increases earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed 12-month averages in the same quarter
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive mean return over the 60-day horizon when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages in the same quarter (t-test p > 0.05).
